minutes.headline: Sewer Commission heard a trailer park owner on manual meters and fees; hearings planned for late Oct and Nov.
minutes.summary: The commission met with the owner and former owner of a mobile home park whose individually read sewer meters the town wants to stop reading, and explained a proposed annual fee and meter standards. Members then discussed irrigation meters, draft policies, a waiver clause, warrant articles for the special town meeting, an engineering RFQ, and legal fee budgeting. They voted to submit warrant articles and the 9/11 minutes were discussed for approval.

public_comment.topic: Mobile home park owner (Wayland/Whalum village) asked about manual meter changes, the proposed annual fee, upgrade costs, connection and reconnect fees, and how costs fall on fixed-income residents.
Former park owner explained why the park installed individual meters, for leak detection, and raised betterment fees charged per unit.
A commissioner reminded listeners the sewer system receives no tax dollars (this was a commissioner statement, not resident comment).

votes.motion: Submit sewer warrant articles (stabilization transfers) with correct numbers before the warrant closes October 9th
Approve minutes of 9/11 (9/18 minutes reviewed but not voted)

budget_items.what_was_said: Draft regulation would charge an annual fee for any meter the town must read or maintain off its system.
Upgrading meters to electronically readable could cost each user additional money.
Park owner said he paid a connection fee again when replacing a mobile home.
Staff said new apartments paid per-building connection fees, negotiated through the zoning board.
Park owner objected to betterment charged per unit.

what_happened.line: The commission voted to submit sewer warrant articles, stabilization transfers, for the November 13 special town meeting, with numbers to be filled in before the warrant closes October 9.
The commission heard the owner and a former owner of a mobile home park on a proposed annual fee for meters the town must read by hand and on meter upgrade costs.
Members deferred a waiver clause to a future agenda, and agreed the draft policy will refer to an 'approved meter' without waiting on a meter definition.
Barb will draft a short RFQ for a maintenance plan and send it to seven engineering firms.
Tentative schedule: public hearings at the end of October and on November 30, a budget meeting November 11, and no meeting December 25.

why_it_matters: Sewer users with individually read meters, including residents of mobile home parks, could face a new annual fee or meter upgrade costs if the draft regulation is adopted.

The stabilization transfers on the November 13 special town meeting warrant are a vote residents will be asked to take, and the commission's statement that the sewer system receives no tax dollars means these costs fall on sewer users.
watch_next: Warrant closes October 9 for the November 13 special town meeting; transfer numbers are to be filled in after FY18 close.
Public hearings on the draft meter policy at the end of October and on November 30, with the budget meeting November 11.
